Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2015 Manifesto

## Economic Policy
The document outlines a plan to eliminate the budget deficit through continued spending reductions and welfare savings, while protecting health service funding. The goal is to achieve a budget surplus by 2018-19 and begin reducing national debt. Commitments include no increases to VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax rates, while raising the tax-free personal allowance to £12,500 and the higher rate threshold to £50,000.

## Regional Development
Plans include significant infrastructure investment across regions, including transport improvements for the North, Midlands, South West, and East of England. Devolution of powers to cities choosing elected mayors is proposed, alongside retention of business rates locally to incentivize growth.

## Infrastructure
The document commits over £100 billion for infrastructure, including railway electrification, high-speed rail development, road improvements, and broadband expansion to 95% coverage by 2017. Mobile coverage improvements and 5G development are also prioritized.

## Employment and Business
Targets include creating two million jobs, three million apprenticeships, and achieving full employment. Policies aim to support small businesses through rate reviews, reduced regulation, and improved access to finance. Youth unemployment would be addressed through mandatory work requirements for benefit claimants aged 18-21.

## Welfare Reform
The household benefit cap would reduce to £23,000 annually. Universal Credit rollout continues, with working-age benefits frozen for two years. The document emphasizes making work financially preferable to benefits.

## Immigration
Proposals include requiring EU migrants to work four years before accessing certain benefits, restricting housing benefit for EU jobseekers, and ending child benefit payments for children living abroad. Enhanced enforcement and border controls are outlined.

## Education
Commitments include maintaining per-pupil funding, expanding academies and free schools, and opening at least 500 new free schools. University places would be uncapped, and apprenticeship programs expanded.

## Healthcare
The National Health Service would receive minimum £8 billion additional funding over five years. Goals include seven-day GP and hospital access, same-day appointments for over-75s, and integration of health and social care services. Mental health services would receive increased funding.

## Housing
Targets include 200,000 starter homes at 20% below market price for first-time buyers under 40, extending Right to Buy to housing association tenants, and introducing Help to Buy ISAs. Green Belt protections would continue.

## Pensions and Elderly Care
The triple lock on state pensions continues, guaranteeing increases of at least 2.5% annually. Residential care costs would be capped, inheritance tax thresholds effectively raised to £1 million for couples, and pensioner benefits including bus passes and winter fuel payments maintained.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include English votes for English laws, implementing devolution agreements for Scotland and Wales, boundary reforms reducing MPs to 600, and continued implementation of agreements in Northern Ireland.

## Foreign Policy and Defence
Armed forces would maintain current size, with Trident nuclear deterrent renewed. Defence spending would meet NATO's 2% target. International development spending would remain at 0.7% of national income.

## Environment and Energy
Commitments include ending subsidies for onshore wind farms, supporting shale gas development, creating marine protection zones, and investing in flood defences. Climate change commitments under existing legislation would continue.
